{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "For 'Success', since the data is binary (0/1), perform a Chi-square test of independence or a logistic regression ANOVA (GLM with binomial family) instead of standard ANOVA, as normality assumptions will be violated.",
    "For 'Path Efficiency', inspect the distribution; if highly skewed (suggested by mean=0.47, sd=0.46, min=0.0009), consider a log-transformation or non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test before proceeding with ANOVA.",
    "For 'Time-to-Target', 'Average Speed', and 'AD', proceed with standard one-way ANOVA if normality and homogeneity of variance assumptions are met after inspection."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Check residuals for each paradigm group using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests; note that 'Success' is inherently non-normal.",
    "Homogeneity of Variance: Conduct Levene's test for equality of variances across the five paradigms for each continuous variable.",
    "Independence: Verify that observations (rows) are independent trials; check for repeated measures within the same 'Mouse' ID if the design implies within-subject comparisons.",
    "Outliers: Inspect boxplots for extreme values, particularly in 'Time-to-Target' (max=201.39) and 'Average Speed' (max=75.35), which may influence the omnibus F-test."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If the omnibus ANOVA F-statistic is significant (p < 0.05), conduct post-hoc pairwise comparisons using Tukey's HSD (Honest Significant Difference) test to control the family-wise error rate.",
    "For 'Success', use pairwise comparisons of proportions (e.g., Fisher's Exact Test or Bonferroni-corrected z-tests) if the GLM/Chi-square indicates a significant effect.",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., eta-squared for ANOVA, Cohen's h for proportions) for all significant pairwise differences.",
    "Specifically compare 'Sham' against all other paradigms given the large mean difference in 'Success' (0.27 vs ~0.68-0.78) and 'Time-to-Target' (4.68 vs ~2.5-3.1)."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Based on summary statistics, 'Sham' is expected to show significantly worse performance than all other paradigms in 'Success' (0.27 vs ~0.7) and 'Time-to-Target' (4.68 vs ~2.5-3.1).",
    "'Path Efficiency' and 'AD' are expected to differ significantly, with 'Sham' showing lower efficiency (0.31) and lower AD (0.24) compared to others, though the interpretation of AD direction depends on the specific metric definition (lower AD usually implies less dispersion/better performance, but here Sham has the lowest value while having the worst success, suggesting potential confounding or different behavioral strategies).",
    "'Average Speed' is expected to be lower in 'Sham' (10.74) compared to 'Combined' (12.83) and 'ICMS Only' (12.04), indicating slower navigation in the control group.",
    "The 'Combined' paradigm may show the best overall performance profile (high success, low time-to-target, high efficiency)."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset contains a highly imbalanced number of observations per paradigm (Sham n=3505 vs Combined n=48846), which can affect the power of the ANOVA and the validity of homogeneity of variance tests.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary, violating the normality assumption required for standard ANOVA, necessitating a different statistical approach.",
    "Potential confounding by 'Mouse' ID: If multiple trials per mouse exist, the independence assumption of standard ANOVA is violated, requiring a mixed-effects model instead.",
    "Extreme outliers in 'Time-to-Target' (up to 201.39) and 'Average Speed' could disproportionately influence the ANOVA results if not transformed or robustly handled."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a mixed-effects logistic regression for 'Success' and mixed-effects linear regression for continuous variables (with appropriate transformations) including 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for within-subject correlation, followed by pairwise contrasts."
}
